title: AITP report-email ready drop
description: The file a run writes into a project's synced folder, LAST and atomically, as `<runId>.ready.json`. A Power Automate flow triggers on it and sends the mail. This schema is what you paste into the flow's Parse JSON step, and tests/unit/ready-schema.spec.ts validates it against what the code actually writes — so the two cannot drift.

schemaVersion.description: Bumped when this shape changes in a way the flow's Parse JSON must notice. A flow should ignore a file whose version it does not know rather than guess at it.

runId.description: The platform's own run id. The file is named after it, so two runs finishing close together cannot overwrite each other.

app.description: The application slug — the config/apps/<slug> directory this run belongs to.

environment.description: The environment key: `local`, `qa`, `app`. NOT the application — one application has several.

ranBy.description: The address the mail says it is from. Its DOMAIN is the only domain recipients may be in; the flow re-checks that, because this file is editable by hand.

to.description: At least one. A drop with no recipient would be picked up and sent to nobody — a silent success, which is why the platform refuses to write one.

cc.description: May be empty. Delivered exactly like `to`, so the flow applies the same domain filter to it.

subject.description: [<APP>] <environment> run — <passed> passed, <failed> failed (<duration>) — <ranBy>. Already formatted; the flow sends it verbatim.

verdict.description: Derived from counts.failed, not from a status field, so it cannot disagree with the numbers below it.

counts.description: Per TEST, not per execution: a retried test is counted once. The body's table has one row per attempt and says so.

bodyHtml.description: A complete, self-contained HTML document with inline styles and table layout, built for Outlook's Word rendering engine. No <style> block, no script, no remote images. The flow puts it in the mail body as-is.

bodyText.description: The same report as plain text, for the multipart fallback: a watch, a screen reader, a plain-text client and a gateway that strips HTML all show this one. OPTIONAL and additive — a ready file written before this field existed has no 'bodyText', so the flow must coalesce it rather than assume it. The same text is also summary.md inside the bundle.

importance.description: Outlook's Importance header. 'High' when failed > 0, 'Normal' otherwise — keyed on failures and NOT on the verdict, because a run that passed after a retry is worth reading and is not worth interrupting somebody for. OPTIONAL and additive: coalesce to 'Normal' in the flow, or an older ready file sends with no importance at all.

reportZipName.description: The archive's file name, sitting in the SAME folder as this file, or null when no archive was written. Never an empty string: the flow needs to tell 'no archive' from 'a field that was dropped'.

reportZipTooLarge.description: True when an archive exists but is over 10 MB. The body already says so; the flow should NOT attach it, because a mail gateway silently dropping a paperclip is the failure this field exists to avoid.
